subject: Post-call: Budget constraints, token levers, and pilot gating criteria
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@clearpay.com>; Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@paymentslab.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: budget constraints, token levers, and pilot gating criteria

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great conversation. I wanted to capture the key points and recommended next steps so we have a single place to act from.

High-level summary
- Primary pain: unpredictable token spend on NLU features (chat + reranking) causing monthly budget overruns.
- Business goal: bring token unit cost within a 30% delta of current infra spend while improving user engagement by enabling richer chat.
- Constraints: procurement cap of ~€75k for POC (3 months), security questionnaires pending but not blocking the pilot.

Technical levers we discussed
- Batching and KV cache: likely 20–35% token reduction on inference for your current seq lengths (avg 180 tokens) if we enable continuous batching + prefix caching.
- Model family tradeoff: recommend starting with a 7B quantized variant for parity tests, fallback to 13B only for high-value flows. Estimated delta: ~1.6x tokens processed for 13B vs 7B.
- Prompt and evals: define 12 canonical prompts for quality gates (we'll run automatic regressions on Redwood Optimize).

Proposed pilot scope (3 months)
- Objective: validate engagement uplift with cost per MAU below €0.08 while keeping latency <250ms p50.
- Ramp plan: sandbox -> canary (week 3) -> full pilot at 50% traffic (week 6).
- Ops: Redwood provides tracing hooks, token-level cost dashboards, and a one-off batch tuning pass.

Budget framing and options
- Ballpark unit economics: baseline estimate attached (pilot_pricing_quote.pdf) showing projected per-token and per-MAU costs under three batching assumptions.
- If procurement cap holds at €75k we recommend: reserved burst capacity + 10% discount for pilot commitment to guarantee predictability.

Next steps (action owners)
- Samir: confirm procurement window and any internal approval dates (by 2027-09-06).
- Elena: share security questionnaire status (SOC2 items outstanding) and whether a VPN/VPC is required.
- Marissa & I: prepare a scoped pricing quote and mutual action plan (attached) for signature.

Attachments: pilot_pricing_quote.pdf (pdf, 3 pages) ; mutual_action_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — I'll follow up with a short one-page cost snapshot for your CFO.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@clearpay.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@paymentslab.io>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: budget constraints, token levers, and pilot gating criteria

Diego — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Procurement cap: the €75k is the current ask from Finance for third-party pilots. We can stretch to €90k with VP approval but that requires a one pager showing expected MAU impact.
2) Security: SOC2 in progress; we have a few outstanding items around audit logs and encryption-at-rest. We do prefer VPC for pilots handling PII, but for this first POC we could delay VPC to month 2 if needed.
3) Cost ask: can you provide an amortized cost per MAU (monthly) under the three batching scenarios? Finance will want a simple table: conservative / expected / optimistic.

Also looping in Elena — she'll coordinate security artifacts and help prioritize prompts for the eval set.

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearPay

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: budget constraints, token levers, and pilot gating criteria

Looping in our commercial and solutions leads with a concrete recommendation.

Diego / team — draft proposal attached (pilot_pricing_quote.pdf) with three pricing bands tied to batching: conservative (no batching), expected (conservative caching + basic batching), optimistic (aggressive continuous batching + KV cache). Highlights:
- With expected batching we model ~28% reduction in billable tokens vs current run-rate.
- To meet the €75k cap for a 3-month POC at expected batching we recommend a pilot commit of €65k + a 10% usage buffer credit.
- We can include an SLA clause for latency and a rollback plan to a smaller model family to tighten spend if quality/regressions appear.

Action items I've taken on:
- Attached mutual_action_plan.xlsx with milestones and signoffs (kickoff, security handoff, canary date).
- Preparing a one-page CFO-friendly cost-per-MAU table (conservative/expected/optimistic) — will send by EOD PST.

Samir — can you confirm whether Finance needs the amortized MAU view as gross MAU or only MAU tied to chat flows? That will change the denominator.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Confirming next steps from our side:
- Finance will accept the €75k pilot with the buffer credit option; I will need the CFO one-pager by 2027-09-03 COB.
- Security: Elena is collecting the SOC2 artifacts and will confirm whether VPC can be deferred.
- Legal: we'll need a limited scope MSA addendum for the pilot (I can share our template, will do by tomorrow).

Scheduling
- Tentative kickoff: 2027-09-13 (internal alignment 9/10). Please block a 60-min kickoff and include the SRE/infra lead.

I’m happy with the pricing bands shown — once we have the CFO one-pager and the amortized MAU table we can move to signature.

Samir
